## Your turn {.smaller}

**Exercise (⭐).** Add a **diversification** rule to the mean-variance problem: no
single asset may exceed 25% of the budget. Re-solve at $\gamma = 10$ and compare with
the unconstrained allocation.

::: {.notes}
**Solution (presenter notes).**

A position cap is one linear constraint, `w <= 0.25`:
```r
base <- Problem(Maximize(ret - 10 * risk), cons)
capd <- Problem(Maximize(ret - 10 * risk), c(cons, list(w <= 0.25)))
psolve(base); w0 <- value(w)
psolve(capd); w1 <- value(w)
data.frame(asset = names(mu),
           uncapped = round(w0, 3),
           capped   = round(w1, 3))[round(w0,3) > 0 | round(w1,3) > 0, ]
```
The cap spreads weight off the assets that the unconstrained solution concentrated in
--- a one-line way to encode an investment policy.
:::
